title: Adult Male Height by Birth Cohort (1896–1996)
publisher: NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (NCD-RisC) / Our World in Data
latest_value: 1996 birth cohort: PRK 172.0 cm vs ROK 174.9 cm (ROK +2.9 cm gap; in 1896 PRK was taller at 160.6 cm vs ROK 159.8 cm)
compare: ROK (174.9 cm), China (175.7 cm), Japan (170.8 cm), World (171.1 cm)
presentation: OWID presents global birth-cohort curves. Shows historic crossover around the 1940 birth cohort when South Korean male stature overtook North Korea and widened.
chart_idea: The Physical Divide: How South Korean men evolved from shorter than Northerners in 1896 to 3 cm taller today.
notes: Verified against live OWID grapher API and NCD-RisC 2016 Lancet dataset. Covers 101 consecutive birth cohorts measured at age 18 (1914–2014).

title: Adult Female Height by Birth Cohort (1896–1996)
publisher: NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (NCD-RisC) / Our World in Data
latest_value: 1996 birth cohort: PRK 159.0 cm vs ROK 162.3 cm (South Korean women surged +20.2 cm over a century vs DPRK +9.8 cm)
compare: ROK (162.3 cm), Japan (158.3 cm), China (163.5 cm), World (159.5 cm)
presentation: OWID displays global female height trends. South Korean women achieved the largest female height gain of any population on Earth (+20.2 cm), while North Korean gains stalled.
chart_idea: A Century of Female Stature: South Korean women gained 20.2 cm in 100 years—the fastest gain on earth—leaving North Korean peers 3.4 cm behind.
notes: Verified against OWID. In 1896, North Korean women averaged 149.1 cm while South Korean women were only 142.2 cm (-6.9 cm). By 1996, South Korea surged ahead to 162.3 cm.

title: North Korean Defector Height and Stunting Disparity
publisher: Ministry of Unification (MOU) / Pak Sunyoung (2010) / Schwekendiek (2009)
latest_value: Famine cohort arrivals: Adult defectors average 3-6 cm shorter; adolescent defectors arrived 8-13 cm shorter than South Korean age peers
compare: ROK national youth school physical examination standards
presentation: Scattered across Hanawon orientation medical intake reports, academic anthropometry journals, and MOU whitepapers.
chart_idea: The Stunting Legacy of the 1990s Famine: Height gap between North Korean escapees and South Korean peers by age at arrival.
notes: Pak Sunyoung (2010, Annals of Human Biology) examined 2,750 refugees; Schwekendiek (2009) confirmed pre-school and school-age North Korean children lagged South Korean peers by over 2 standard deviations in height and weight.

title: North Korea Wigs & False Eyelashes Exports to China (HS 6704)
publisher: UN Comtrade / General Administration of Customs of China (GACC)
latest_value: 2024: $187,772,505 USD (3,575.6 metric tons) — DPRK's #1 processed export to China
compare: Coal exports ($0), Iron ore ($0), Total DPRK exports to China ($347M)
presentation: Buried inside UN Comtrade 6-digit tariff tables. Shows dramatic post-COVID boom: $372k in 2021 -> $166.7M in 2023 -> $187.8M in 2024 (now ~54% of all DPRK exports to China).
chart_idea: The Eyelash Pivot: How false eyelashes became North Korea's biggest export after sanctions wiped out coal and textiles.
notes: Verified directly via UN Comtrade API preview. Chinese cosmetic processors in Dandong and Qingdao subcontract eyelash knotting and wig weaving to North Korean labor, circumventing UN bans on commercial minerals and apparel.

title: North Korea Coal Exports to China (HS 2701)
publisher: UN Comtrade / General Administration of Customs of China
latest_value: 2024: $0 USD (collapsed from $1,186,694,713 in 2016 under UNSCR 2371)
compare: HS 6704 Wigs ($187.8M in 2024), Pre-sanctions peak trade
presentation: Displayed as standard trade ledger. Captures the total annihilation of North Korea's primary hard currency export under UN Security Council Resolution 2371.
chart_idea: The Sanctions Cliff: How North Korea's $1.2B coal trade went to zero in 18 months.
notes: Verified via UN Comtrade: 2016 was $1.19B (7.75M tons), 2017 dropped to $410.4M (4.91M tons), 2018-2024 officially $0. Clandestine ship-to-ship transfers continue off Ningbo/Zhoushan but are excluded from official customs.

title: North Korea Iron Ore Exports to China (HS 2601)
publisher: UN Comtrade / General Administration of Customs of China
latest_value: 2024: $0 USD (collapsed from $103,370,110 in 2017 under UNSCR 2371)
compare: Musan Iron Mine estimated production capacity
presentation: Raw customs table showing abrupt drop from 1.66M tons in 2017 to exactly 0 in 2018.
chart_idea: Severing the Ore Line: Official Chinese imports of North Korean iron ore plunging to zero.
notes: Verified via UN Comtrade API preview. Musan mine was previously connected by dedicated slurry pipeline and cross-border rail into Jilin province.

title: North Korea Apparel & Garment Exports to China (HS 61 & 62)
publisher: UN Comtrade / General Administration of Customs of China
latest_value: 2024: $0 USD (collapsed from $561,787,103 in 2017 across HS 61+62 under UNSCR 2375)
compare: Woven apparel (HS 62: $496.5M in 2017 -> $0), Knitted apparel (HS 61: $65.3M in 2017 -> $0)
presentation: Standard trade database. Details the extinction of DPRK's second largest foreign exchange generator (toll garment manufacturing).
chart_idea: The Vanished Factories: North Korea's half-billion-dollar textile export industry before and after UNSCR 2375.
notes: Verified via UN Comtrade API. Combined HS 61 + HS 62 totaled $561.3M in 2016 and $561.8M in 2017 before collapsing to under $20,000 in 2018 and zero thereafter.

title: North Korea Fish & Aquatic Invertebrate Exports to China (HS 03)
publisher: UN Comtrade / General Administration of Customs of China
latest_value: 2024: $0 USD (collapsed from $190,344,448 in 2016 and $163,029,081 in 2017 under UNSCR 2371)
compare: Global Fishing Watch estimated illegal squid catch ($165M-$275M/yr)
presentation: Customs ledger showing complete collapse of seafood exports from August 2017 onwards.
chart_idea: From Legal Seafood Exports to Dark Fleet Poaching: How the $190M seafood trade vanished from customs into illicit open-sea harvesting.
notes: Verified via UN Comtrade API. UNSCR 2371 passed in August 2017 banned all exports of fish, crustaceans, molluscs, and aquatic invertebrates from DPRK.

title: Cross-Border Electrical Energy Trade (HS 2716)
publisher: UN Comtrade / China Customs / State Grid
latest_value: 2024: ~$10M-$12M annual balancing transactions (250,000-300,000 MWh) under Sup'ung Dam 50/50 treaty
compare: Sup'ung Dam total installed generation capacity (700 MW)
presentation: Shown as HS 2716 tariff category in mirror customs. Demonstrates unbroken physical energy infrastructure linking the two states.
chart_idea: The Power Grid That Sanctions Couldn't Unplug: North Korea and China's continuous electricity trade from the Sup'ung Dam.
notes: Verified via UN Comtrade API: 2016 ($5.76M), 2017 ($10.98M), 2018 ($11.39M), 2019 ($11.43M). Governed by the 1955 Yalu River Hydroelectric Corporation agreement.

title: Total Chinese Imports from North Korea (Mirror DPRK Exports)
publisher: UN Comtrade / General Administration of Customs of China (GACC)
compare: Chinese exports to DPRK ($1,833,000,000 in 2024 — $1.48B trade deficit)
presentation: Top-level annual customs total. Captures the profound contraction and post-pandemic restructuring of North Korea's external economic relations.
chart_idea: The Great Squeeze: Total Chinese imports from North Korea from $2.6B in 2016 to the post-COVID eyelash plateau.
notes: Verified via GACC and UN Comtrade. China accounts for over 95% of North Korea's total recorded external merchandise trade.

title: North Korean Drifting Wooden Boats Found in Japan (漂流・漂着木造船等の確認件数)
publisher: Japan Coast Guard (海上保安庁) / Ministry of Foreign Affairs (外務省)

compare: DPRK seafood sanctions timeline, COVID border closure

chart_idea: Ghost Ships of the Sea of Japan: How sanctions and regime quotas drove a surge in North Korean wooden boats washing ashore in Japan.

title: Dark Fleet Illegal Squid Catch in North Korean Waters
publisher: Global Fishing Watch / Science Advances (Park et al. 2020)
latest_value: 2024: ~510 vessels detected, ~46,000 metric tons ($125M USD); cumulative >164k tons ($440M+) in 2017-2018 alone
compare: South Korea legal squid catch, Japan legal squid catch
presentation: Analyzed through multi-satellite sensor fusion (AIS, SAR, VIIRS night lights) in landmark Science Advances paper and GFW Map.
chart_idea: The Ghost Armada: Over 900 dark fishing trawlers illegally harvesting $440M of squid from sanctioned North Korean waters.
notes: Park et al. 2020 (DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.abb1197). Revealed the largest known case of illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing by a single distant-water fleet, directly explaining the displacement and deaths of North Korean artisanal fishers.

title: Sinuiju Weather Station Annual Mean Temperature (KNM00047035)
publisher: NOAA NCEI Global Historical Climatology Network (GHCN-Daily) / WMO
latest_value: 2024: 11.96°C (record warm year; warming trend of +1.8°C over 1960s baseline of 10.1°C)
compare: Dandong (China), Pyongyang, Seoul
presentation: Raw fixed-width daily archive (.dly format). Continuously updated daily through current month (September 2026).
chart_idea: Climate Change on the Yalu: 67 years of daily weather station observations at Sinuiju showing steep upward temperature acceleration.
notes: Verified by parsing KNM00047035.dly: 3,121 lines covering 1957 to September 2026. 2024 was the hottest calendar year recorded in the station's history (11.96°C mean, 353 days observed).

title: Sinuiju Daily Precipitation & Historic July 2024 Flood Event
publisher: NOAA NCEI GHCN-Daily / WMO Station 47035

compare: Historical flood years (1995, 2010, 2018)

chart_idea: The Deluge That Flooded Sinuiju: Daily rainfall spike of July 2024 in Sinuiju compared to historical monsoon distributions.
notes: Verified from GHCN-Daily record: July 2024 days 25-29 recorded 34.0mm, 20.1mm, 126.0mm, 11.9mm, 29.2mm. Led Kim Jong Un to deploy military rescue helicopters and dismiss top officials.

title: Pyongyang Sunan Weather Station Annual Mean Temperature (KNM00047058)

compare: Seoul (13.7°C), Tokyo (16.2°C), Global average anomaly

chart_idea: Warming the Capital: 75 years of official daily temperature records at Pyongyang Sunan International Airport.
notes: Verified from KNM00047058.dly: 1950–2025 continuous observations. Annual means: 2016 (11.64°C), 2020 (11.56°C), 2023 (12.28°C), 2024 (13.06°C).

title: Estimated Assembled Nuclear Warhead Arsenal (2015–2026)

publisher: IPFM / FAS / IAEA Director General Reports

chart_idea: The Plutonium Ceiling: How Yongbyon's small 5MWe reactor created a flat plateau in North Korea's plutonium inventory.
notes: Verified from IPFM reports. Yongbyon 5MWe reactor produces approximately 6 kg of plutonium per year when operating at full thermal capacity.

title: North Korea Highly Enriched Uranium (HEU) Stockpile
publisher: IPFM / FAS / ISIS (David Albright) / ROK Defense Intelligence Agency

chart_idea: The Centrifuge Escalation: The exponential growth of North Korea's highly enriched uranium stockpile.
notes: Verified against FAS and ROK DIA assessments. North Korea operates an estimated 4,000-6,000 P-2 centrifuges, producing ~150-200 kg HEU annually.
